newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude soft, Med buyers spoilt for choice.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude soft, Med buyers spoilt for choice.

text.p: Late March cargoes kept Dated Brent depressed on Tuesday and slack early April demand for other North Sea grades sidelined sellers hoping for an improvement in differentials, traders said.
Two late March Brents traded at May Brent -70 and -68 cents, a shade softer than Monday's deals at April -80 and -81 cents.
Traders said the March overhang was still weighing heavily on North Sea crudes despite an improvement in refining margins.
"There are still a few March cargoes around and it's not a good situation to be in...I don't see any reason to be optimistic at the moment," said a North Sea seller.
"If you look at April 1-10, it's not really got started yet," he added.
While most North Sea sellers were keen to wait for any sign of improvement in differentials for April stems, March cargoes continued to move at lower numbers.
A Statfjord loading March 24-26 traded at Dated Brent +5 cents, down five cents from the level achieved on Monday for an April 1-3 cargo.
Only gasoline-rich Forties was seen holding its value amid unconfirmed talk of a deal at Dated Brent +10 cents.
"It's the grade for the time of year," said a trader.
Paper Brent intermonth spreads were steady to a shade firmer, helped by gains in outright futures values. May/June traded at +9 cents, 1-2 cents firmer than earlier in the day.
Two Brent cargoes loading April 2-4 were kept by British Petroleum, who already held the two April 1-3 stems.
Sour crude barrels from Russia, the Middle East and Latin America were raining down on a reluctant Mediterranean market on Tuesday, turning up the pressure on differentials.
Benchmark Russian Urals was offered as low as Dated Brent -$1.30 a barrel after a cargo loading in late March changed hands on Monday at Dated Brent -$1.24.
